subject: MAP draft: Load/perf test slot and responsibilities
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <sam.lee@finapps.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@finapps.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft: Load/perf test slot and responsibilities

Hi Samantha / Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed MAP milestone focused on the load/perf validation so we can lock a slot and clear dependencies.

Summary (from today)
- Goal: Run a traffic-replay-based peak QPS validation to confirm dedicated capacity sizing and SLA headroom ahead of pilot.
- Scope: Replay production traffic slice (last 30 days, anonymized) at peak concurrency and peak burst patterns; target token-length distribution ~avg 420 tokens.

Proposed MAP milestone: "Load/Perf Validation"
- Target window options (please confirm preferred): 1) Jun 14-17 (preferred) or 2) May 31-Jun 4 (fallback)
- Success criteria: 95th pctl latency < 600ms for text-gen baseline and < 1s for tool-calling flows; error rate < 0.5% sustained during peak.
- Responsible owners:
  - FinApps (provide replay dataset + traffic pattern CSV): Samantha Lee (FinApps)
  - Redwood (run test, capacity sizing, and monitoring): Ben Carter (Redwood)
  - Joint post-test review and action items: Priya Natarajan (Redwood) & Marissa Cole (Redwood)
- Dependencies:
  1) FinApps shares sanitized traffic capture (CSV + sample traces) and a test account by Jun 4
  2) Procurement sign-off for dedicated pool (if required) — procurement contact: Tom
  3) Access to target environment/network allowlist (IP ranges)
- Preliminary capacity ask (for planning): 3–4 large GPU nodes or equivalent (estimate attached). Final sizing depends on peak QPS we see in the replay.

Attached: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (MAP milestone text), traffic-patterns.csv (format sample), capacity-estimate.xlsx (initial sizing model).

Next steps I propose:
1) Samantha/Tom: confirm preferred test window by EOD Wed (May 26) and share expected peak QPS or earliest sample dataset.
2) Ben: validate sizing model and flag any infra lead time.
3) Priya/Marissa: finalize MAP with dates and update HubSpot.

If the Jun 14-17 window works, we’ll treat that as our MAP milestone target and target closing the pilot contract by Jun 30.

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <sam.lee@finapps.com>

Subject: Re: MAP draft: Load/perf test slot and responsibilities

Thanks Priya — good summary. We are aligned on the objective. A few quick answers/questions:

- Preferred window: Jun 14-17 looks good on our side. We can move May 31-Jun 4 if there’s a blocking dependency, but Jun 14-17 is preferred.
- Peak QPS: our production telemetry shows peak ~1,100 requests/sec (90th) for the conversational route; bursts up to ~1,600 rps for short spikes. Average token length roughly 420 as you noted.
- Dataset: I can share an anonymized traffic capture and the sample CSV by Thu (May 27). Will need a checklist from your team for required fields (session id, timestamp, route, prompt+metadata).
- Procurement: Tom is looping in procurement; we’ll know if a dedicated capacity PO is required by Jun 2.

One ask: can Redwood confirm whether we must commit to dedicated nodes for the replay or whether a temporary reserved pool (2–3 days) is sufficient to emulate production? If dedicated is mandatory, we’ll need procurement lead time.

I’ll upload the sample CSV to the shared drive once it’s scrubbed.

—Sam

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <sam.lee@finapps.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@finapps.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft: Load/perf test slot and responsibilities

Thanks — quick technical note for sizing and the procurement question.

Short answer on dedicated vs reserved: for an accurate capacity validation we prefer a dedicated pool (isolated GPUs) for the replay window. Shared clusters introduce noise that can mask tail latency and queueing under peak QPS. That said, if procurement timeline prevents a dedicated pool, we can run a controlled reservation on multi-tenant nodes with tighter telemetry and longer ramp phases; results will be directional but less definitive.

Sizing guidance (preliminary):
- Based on 1,100 rps sustained and average 420 tokens, assume ~1.2M tokens/min at peak. For the model family you’re evaluating (LlamaX-70B quantized), our back-of-envelope: 3 x 80GB A100-equivalent GPUs for baseline with 1.2x headroom for bursts. If you expect sustained 1,600 rps bursts, plan 4 nodes.
- If you want a safety margin for non-deterministic tool-calls and longer sequences, add one extra node as buffer.

Operational asks (to run the test):
1) FinApps: upload anonymized traffic CSV and sample traces by Fri (May 27). Include expected auth method, IP allowlist, and any rate-limiting rules we should mirror.
2) FinApps: test account and test API key with the same model selection and routing rules.
3) Redwood: we will provision infra and smoke-test the pipeline 48 hours before the replay window.

I’ve updated the capacity-estimate.xlsx and attached a quick worksheet. I’ll schedule a short infra sync if you want to walk through the numbers — 30 minutes should suffice.

—Ben

Next steps for this thread: Sam to confirm dataset delivery on Thu; Tom to flag procurement timeline by Jun 2 — if both are green, we’ll convert MAP milestone to an active task in HubSpot and send an invite for the infra smoke-test slot.

Thanks again — looking forward to the run.
